name: Baron Silverlaine
summary: Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Keep Silverlaine, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron and his household were mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb.

sections.title: The Fall of Keep Silverlaine
sections.body: Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding Gilnean lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron along with his entire family.

sections.title: A Tormented Specter
sections.body: Death brought no release to Baron Silverlaine. Bound to the keep's ancient Great Hall, his restless ghost now wanders the trashed dining tables where he once feasted. The cursed lord lashes out at intruders who enter his ruined home.

faq.answer: He was the noble Gilnean human master of the fortress originally named Keep Silverlaine, situated above Pyrewood Village. He was slain alongside his family when worgen overran the fortress.

faq.q: Why is he haunting Shadowfang Keep?
faq.answer: Silverlaine was slaughtered in his own home during the worgen onslaught unleashed by Archmage Arugal. Cursed in death, his ghost remains tethered to the dining hall of his ruined keep, unable to move on.
His cursed spirit remains within his former home, where he attacks trespassers in the Great Hall.

faq.q: Where in the keep can he be found?
faq.answer: Baron Silverlaine haunts the Great Hall, which served as the keep's lavish dining room before it was wrecked during the fall of his estate.

faq.q: What was Shadowfang Keep called before the worgen attack?
faq.answer: It was originally called Keep Silverlaine, named after the baron's noble family who held dominion over it before Arugal took control.

faq.q: Did anyone in Silverlaine's family survive?
faq.answer: No. Historical accounts confirm that Baron Silverlaine and his entire family were slaughtered inside the keep when the feral worgen invaded.

angles.text: Silverlaine stands as a bitter testament to the downfall of human noble authority on the borders of Gilneas, his family wiped out by the magical hubris of a Dalaran-trained wizard.
For the Forsaken pushing across Silverpine, Silverlaine's specter is merely another remnant of old Gilnean aristocracy that must be cleared to break Arugal's grip on the keep.
Silverlaine's fate serves as a grim warning of magical recklessness; the summoner's art, when mishandled as Archmage Arugal did, destroys innocent lives and leaves indelible scars.
